Both are now sourced: APEC's 2015 Framework says the 2005 version 'was modelled upon the OECD Guidelines (1980)', and the PCPD says Hong Kong's Law Reform Commission recommended a law 'based on the OECD Privacy Guidelines 1980'. Both quotes FOUND.

fieldFixes.note: The OECD calls them 'the first internationally agreed-upon set of privacy principles', although the Council of Europe had adopted resolutions on data-bank privacy principles in 1973 and 1974. There are eight principles: collection limitation, data quality, purpose specification, use limitation, security safeguards, openness, individual participation and accountability. APEC's first Privacy Framework was 'modelled upon' them, as was Hong Kong's 1995 ordinance, which followed a law-reform recommendation for a law 'based on the OECD Privacy Guidelines 1980'. The OECD says they have influenced legislation 'in OECD countries and beyond'.

issues: Overstated causal claim. The note said Article 25 'pushed Argentina, Uruguay, Israel, New Zealand and others toward EU-style laws'. The Commission's own adequacy decisions show that at least two of those laws predate the Directive. The New Zealand decision (2013/65/EU) says the Privacy Act 'predates Directive 95/46/EC' (it was amended in 2010). The Israel decision (2011/61/EU) says Israel's standards are laid down in the 'Privacy Protection Act 5741-1981, lastly amended in 2007'. The adequacy findings themselves are confirmed: Argentina (2003/490/EC), Israel (2011/61/EU of 31 January 2011), Uruguay (2012/484/EU of 21 August 2012) and New Zealand (2013/65/EU of 19 December 2012). The note is rewritten to state these findings and to drop the blanket causal claim.

'Barred transfers ... without adequate protection' left out Article 26, which lets transfers to non-adequate countries take place under listed conditions ('By way of derogation from Article 25', FOUND). The note now says so.

fieldFixes.note: A directive (binding as to result, transposed by national laws). Its Article 25 allowed personal data to go to a third country only if that country 'ensures an adequate level of protection', with exceptions in Article 26. The Commission later found Argentina (2003), Israel (2011), Uruguay (2012) and New Zealand (2012) adequate, which gave trading partners a commercial reason to adopt or update EU-style laws. Israel's core statute (1981) and New Zealand's Privacy Act predate the Directive, although New Zealand amended its Act in 2010. Covered in detail in the internet slice.

addSources.quote: IN WITNESS WHEREOF WE, THE HEADS OF STATE AND GOVERNMENT OF THE ECONOMIC COMMUNITY OF WEST AFRICAN STATES HAVE SIGNED THIS SUPPLEMENTARY ACT
addSources.note: --check FOUND. The signature block that follows is OCR'd with errors. It shows 13 signatories: Benin, Burkina Faso, Cabo Verde, Côte d'Ivoire, the Gambia, Ghana, Guinea-Bissau, Mali, Liberia, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone and Togo. Article 48: 'This Supplementary Act shall be annexed to the ECOWAS Treaty of which it shall be an integral part' (OCR 'lI1e' for 'the', so it is not checked verbatim).
